solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The cab on circuitous route certainly can!

indicators.note: a cab on a circuitous route wanders about, so the letters of the words are taken on a roundabout path into a new order

explanation.surface: A passenger insists a taxi taking the long way round is perfectly able to get there.
explanation.definitionFit: Betcha is slangy speech for 'bet you', an emphatic assurance, as in 'Betcha I can!', so it stands for certainly can.

clue.text: Second plane on which one's seated

parts.note: to second someone is to back or support them
a side is one plane, or flat face, of a solid figure

explanation.surface: Aircraft talk: a second aeroplane on which one has a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' reads as an aircraft but is a flat face of a figure; 'Second' is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: The backside is the buttocks, the part of the body a person sits on.

clue.text: Group in the morning met up to welcome a bunch of allies

indicators.note: to welcome something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other
in a down entry, going up means the whole run of letters is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a set is a group
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party gathered early to receive someone joining their circle of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the run backwards to give TEMMATES; 'to welcome' then takes A inside. 'met up' looks like a gathering, which hides the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Teammates are people on the same side, a group of allies working together.

clue.text: He produced buzz around priest

indicators.note: the buzzing sound goes around the priest, so the priest sits inside

parts.note: a hum is a buzzing sound
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A man made a humming noise around a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a pronoun for a man but is the chemical symbol for the gas.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the chemical symbol of helium in the periodic table.

clue.text: Glass ship

definitions.meaning: a large tall glass, for sherry or beer
a sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rigging

explanation.definitionFit: Schooner names both a kind of drinking vessel and a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Starter, fresh raita ending in Indian curries

indicators.note: a fresh version is newly made, so these letters are made up anew in another order
the ending of the word Indian is its final letter

explanation.surface: An Indian meal begins with cool new raita before the curries arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a food course in this meal but is the definition: a curtain-raiser opens a theatrical bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain-raiser is a short opening piece before the main play, hence any preliminary event or opener.

clue.text: An oar I broke catching crabs, originally — blow it!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters catch, that is enclose, the next piece
an oar that broke is in pieces, so these letters are rearranged
originally points to the first letter of the word crabs

explanation.surface: A rower snaps an oar while 'catching a crab', a rowing blunder, and curses: blow it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow it!' sounds like an oath but is the definition: an ocarina is something you blow.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, played by blowing into it.

clue.text: Egg on fertiliser

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: An instruction to urge someone towards plant food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' reads as a phrase meaning urge, but the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, potassium nitrate or saltpetre, is used as a fertiliser.

clue.text: Finally, popular singer crossing one European bridge

indicators.note: the letters cross over, that is straddle, the next piece, which ends up inside
finally picks the last letter of the word popular

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A well-liked vocalist walks across a bridge in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous old stone bridge across the Grand Canal in Venice.

clue.text: Stroke head of cat and sensitive tail of mongrel

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of cat

parts.note: raw skin is sensitive, sore

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, here of mongrel

explanation.surface: Pet animals: stroke a cat's head and a dog's touchy tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' looks like a verb about petting but is a swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The crawl is the fast front swimming style, one of the recognised strokes.

clue.text: Drink ale with bather at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone swimming offshore drinks beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbal tea is an infusion of herbs, a hot beverage.

clue.text: Flipping besotted?

definitions.meaning: going ... is turning a somersault, flipping over

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes literally tumbling in a somersault and figuratively being madly in love.

clue.text: Drink umpteen cans for starters during dance

indicators.note: the starters come during the dance, so they sit inside it

parts.note: the samba is a Brazilian dance

indicators.note: starters are the first letters of the words umpteen and cans

explanation.surface: A partygoer downs many tins of beer while dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sambuca is an Italian aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Soldier eats fruit for sustenance

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside, so the fruit is placed within the soldier

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant stands for soldier
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A trooper keeps going on citrus rations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' suggests a military man, but a soldier ant is a caste of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or nourishment.

clue.text: See something on palm?

explanation.walkthrough: 'something on palm' suggests a line read by a palmist, but the palm is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Date means go out with someone and also the fruit of the date palm.

clue.text: Sad not working, actors

parts.note: a system that is down is not working
the cast is the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Performers are gloomy because they are unemployed.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means dejected, low in spirits.

clue.text: Flash like a star?

explanation.definitionFit: A twinkling is a very brief moment, and twinkling describes shining with flickering light.

clue.text: Tablet, perhaps, to cure PM failing

indicators.note: a failing arrangement breaks down, so these letters collapse into a new order

explanation.surface: A pill might cure a Prime Minister who is in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' suggests a pill to cure the ailing PM; it is a tablet computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is one example of a computer, hence 'perhaps' marking the example.

clue.text: Fast bowler going after Surrey's opener, he certainly needs a helmet!

indicators.note: the bowler goes after, so his letters follow the first piece
the opener of a word is its first letter, here of Surrey

parts.note: in cricket a paceman is a fast bowler

explanation.surface: Cricket: a quick bowler facing Surrey's opening batsman, who needs head protection.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county side; a batsman facing pace wears a helmet, but so does an astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceman, an astronaut, must wear a pressurised helmet to survive in space.

clue.text: Boy ending in uniform, literarily opposite?

parts.note: Antony is a boy's name

indicators.note: the ending in a word is its last letter, here of uniform

explanation.surface: A lad finishes in school uniform, set against another in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, so it is opposite in a verbal, literal sense.

clue.text: Initially create image as others see you!

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Advice to craft how you look to the outside world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as others see you' runs on as a phrase, but 'see you!' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is Italian for goodbye, an informal farewell like 'see you'.

clue.text: Peninsula in Brazil, essentially Rio, is astonishing first of all

indicators.note: first of all picks the first letter of every word in the run

explanation.surface: A travel note: at the heart of Brazil, Rio is amazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' suggests a middle letter, but it is only another word whose first letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian Peninsula holds Spain and Portugal in south-west Europe.

clue.text: Something to do with egg? Get out of here!

definitions.meaning: you might beat an egg, so '...' is something to do with one

explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is a command to whisk an egg and also slang ordering someone to leave.

clue.text: Seduce first of chaperones in escort

indicators.note: the letter goes in the escort, inside it

parts.note: to be with someone is to escort or accompany them

indicators.note: first of picks the first letter of the word chaperones

explanation.surface: A chaperone's charge is tempted away by her escort.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch is to enchant or captivate, to win over by charm.

clue.text: Magic cane, did you say?

indicators.note: the question asks whether the word was said, pointing to a word that sounds alike

parts.note: wicker is woven cane, as in wicker furniture

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a wizard's wand.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicca is a modern pagan religion centred on witchcraft and ritual spells.

clue.text: Top found in drink, spit it out!

indicators.note: the top is found inside the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a peak is a top or summit

explanation.surface: Someone finds a bottle cap in their glass and is told to spit it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Speak up is an urging to say clearly what you mean, much like 'spit it out'.

clue.text: Eurocrat upset about new speaker

indicators.note: the reworked letters go about, around, the next piece
an upset arrangement is overturned, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An EU official is annoyed about something new a speaker has said.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled storyteller, someone who speaks entertainingly.

clue.text: Blot isn't seen after a little time

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A stain doesn't show once a short while has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a stain or blemish, a mark on something's character or purity.

clue.text: A gun found in register creating unnecessary panic

indicators.note: the gun is found inside the register

parts.note: a list is a register
an arm is a weapon such as a gun

explanation.surface: A firearm turns up on an official register, causing a scare.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmist describes someone who raises fears without good reason, spreading needless panic.

clue.text: Actor's last, age-related part

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: An actor's final role is one suited to his age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' reads as a theatrical role, but signals letters running inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A stager, usually in 'old stager', is an experienced performer or veteran hand.
